questions.question: Evaluate 3x + 7 when x = 5.
questions.explain: Substitute 5 for x: 3(5) + 7 = 15 + 7 = 22. The most common trap is adding all the numbers (3+5+7=15) instead of multiplying first.

questions.question: Evaluate 2n – 4 when n = 6.
questions.explain: Replace n with 6: 2(6) – 4 = 12 – 4 = 8. Watch out for swapping the coefficient and the variable (n – 2 = 4) or accidentally adding instead of subtracting to get 16.

questions.question: What is the coefficient of x in the expression 5x + 12?
questions.explain: The coefficient is the number multiplied by the variable, so it is 5. Do not confuse it with the constant term (12) or the whole term (5x).

questions.question: Evaluate 4a + 3b when a = 2 and b = 5.
questions.explain: Substitute each value: 4(2) + 3(5) = 8 + 15 = 23. A frequent mistake is swapping the values (4·5 + 3·2 = 26) or simply adding all the numbers together to get 14.

questions.question: A skateboard shop sells a board for $75 and wheels for $40. If you buy n sets of each, the total cost is 75n + 40n. How much do 3 sets cost?
questions.explain: Substitute n = 3 into both terms: 75(3) + 40(3) = 225 + 120 = 345. The most common error is multiplying only one term by n (giving 265 or 195) or just adding 75 + 40.

questions.question: A phone plan costs $30 per month plus $0.25 for each text message. The monthly cost is 30 + 0.25t, where t is the number of texts sent. What is the cost if you send 200 texts?
questions.explain: Substitute t = 200: 30 + 0.25(200) = 30 + 50 = $80. Students often forget the flat $30 (answering $50) or treat every number as if it is being added, getting $230.25.

questions.question: Evaluate 0.5n – 3n + 25 when n = 14.
questions.explain: Substitute 14: 0.5(14) – 3(14) + 25 = 7 – 42 + 25 = –10. The classic trap is flipping a sign, such as writing 7 + 42 – 25 = 24, which changes the meaning of the expression.

questions.question: A delivery driver's pay is 15h + 3d, where h is hours driven and d is the number of deliveries made. If she drives 6 hours and makes 8 deliveries in a day, how much does she earn?
questions.explain: Substitute h = 6 and d = 8: 15(6) + 3(8) = 90 + 24 = $114. Swapping the two values (15·8 + 3·6) gives the tempting but wrong answer of $138.

questions.question: A grocery store gives a 25% loyalty discount. Your bill before the discount is 4p + 2q, where p is the number of premium items and q is the number of regular items. After the discount you pay 0.75(4p + 2q). If you buy 6 premium items and 10 regular items, how much do you pay?
questions.explain: First evaluate the bill: 4(6) + 2(10) = 44. Then apply the 0.75 discount: 0.75 × 44 = $33. A common error is applying the discount to only one group of items, yielding $38 or $39, instead of the whole bill.

questions.question: A BC student earns $10 per hour tutoring but loses $5 each time she forgets to collect her fee. Her weekly pay is 10h – 5f. Last week she tutored 9 hours and forgot to collect 2 fees. What is her pay?
questions.explain: Substitute h = 9 and f = 2: 10(9) – 5(2) = 90 – 10 = $80. The –5f term is a subtraction, so adding it (100) or accidentally using a different value for f (70) are the usual traps.

questions.question: A teen compares two music streaming plans. Plan A costs $12 per month plus $0.50 per song downloaded (cost = 12 + 0.50s). Plan B costs $20 per month with unlimited downloads. If she downloads 30 songs, which plan is cheaper and by how much?
questions.explain: Plan A: 12 + 0.50(30) = 12 + 15 = $27. Plan B: $20. Plan B is cheaper by $7. Students who get the right difference but swap which plan is cheaper, or who conclude they tie, have usually misread which cost is larger.

questions.question: A teenager runs a lemonade stand. Each cup costs $0.15 to make and sells for $2.50. Her profit after making c cups is 2.50c – 0.15c – 8, where $8 is the one-time cost of the stand. If she makes 30 cups, what is her profit?
questions.explain: Substitute c = 30 in every term: 2.50(30) – 0.15(30) – 8 = 75 – 4.50 – 8 = $62.50. The two most common mistakes are dropping the per-cup cost (giving $67) or adding the $8 instead of subtracting it (giving $78.50).
